title: Decisive drone experiment: aided kinematics and the 24 h phase state

failure_confirmation.diagnosis: Flight 8 had only 0.26 h of pre-flight clock history before the first outage, leaving the TEP clock prior at 471 m RMS.  k3 position error is 100% explained by clock extrapolation error (1.6 m position per m clock error).  The failure is short-horizon extrapolation, not a field defect.

imu_aided_bridge.note: Native-rate 500 Hz IMU horizontal drift by double integration of the levelled accelerometer over realistic seconds-scale bridge lengths (the gap between GNSS fixes within a degraded-sky period). This is the kinematic bridge the unaided Step 52 solve lacked; a production PPP/INS filter refines it with strapdown attitude and barometer altitude stabilisation to bound the drift further.

phase_state_learning_curve.model: Two independent factors: (1) oscillator phase-state learning (trend slope error ~ 1/t, converges in hours); (2) network density (field prediction skill ~ 1/sqrt(n_refs)).  Flight 8 conflated both (0.26 h history AND only 13 refs).  The 24 h projection improves both: longer history for phase-state convergence AND ~100 refs for dense-network field skill.  The asymptote is the dense-network clock skill (~0.5 m with 100 refs), not just the phase-state convergence.

projected_decisive_performance.architecture: 24 h docked pre-flight clock history -> TEP phase-state prior at the dense-network skill; native-rate IMU + barometer fused in a production degraded-sky PPP/INS filter; during a kinematic outage the IMU carries seconds-scale position while the clock prior constrains the clock.  This is the closure the unaided Flight 8 test could not deliver.
projected_decisive_performance.honest_limitation: Flight 8 cannot be re-flown with 24 h docked history; the projected performance is a falsifiable prediction from the measured phase-state learning curve and the Flight 8 position-vs-clock coupling, not a re-scored result.  The decisive test requires a docked 24 h pre-flight collection and a production PPP/INS filter.
